Enhancing Early Warning Systems to build greater resilience to hydro-meteorological hazards in Timor-Leste

Annex B - Gender Assessment and Action Plan

1. Introduction: Relevance of Gender Mainstreaming for the Project

This Gender Assessment has been prepared as an input for the design of the Green Climate Fund (GCF) funding proposal by UN Environment Programme (UNEP), titled "Enhancing Early Warning Systems to build greater resilience to hydro-meteorological hazards in Timor-Leste". The project aims at building climate resilience and disaster preparedness capacities at national, sub-national and community level in Timor-Leste through the development of end-of-bend climate and oceans services and impact-based multi-hazard early warning systems. These systems will help communities that are most vulnerable to climate change impacts such as sea level rise, increasing mean temperatures and extreme climatic events, including droughts, floods, landslides, and cyclones.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 | PAGE 18 OF 116

B

## Project Results

### i) Strengthened delivery model and integration for integrated climate information and multi-hazard early warning systems (MHEWS) in Timor-Leste
The project will establish a national climate service (NCS) based on the GFCC to coordinate, facilitate and strengthen collaboration among national institutions for the development of an NCS. The NCS will be established as a focal point for the delivery of the multi-hazard business model of the national meteorological and hydrological service (DMG). Moreover, it will instigate a best practice approach to data governance and advance the integration of climate, health, agriculture, disaster risk reduction, water and environmental management sectors in Timor-Leste.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 PAGE 98 OF 110

## E

This Activity will build the capacity of Timor-Leste to prepare for and respond to the impacts of climate change risks and health impacts. The Project will work with the Civil Protection Unit (CPL) - Timor- Leste, the National Directorate for Climate Change (DNCC), and the National Directorate for Disaster Management (NDM) to enhance disaster preparedness through capacity building at national level for early warning systems (EWS) and community-level for disaster risk management and co-ordination.

In addition, The Project will conduct a targeted disaster risk awareness and education campaign for women, which will focus on empowering women with the understanding and knowledge for improved disaster risk management and decision-making for climate resilience.

### 4.1 - Build capacity to prepare for and respond to risks and hazards

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 | PAGE 81 OF 110

## Timor-Leste's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) (2021-2030)
As noted above, the Project is identified as a priority in the NAP and the Timor-Leste National Adaptation Strategy (NLNAS). In addition to contributing to the achievement of the following priorities and outcomes: * Strengthening the capacity of national, local institutions and communities in managing climate risks; * Reducing the vulnerability of communities to climate change impacts through increased resilience at all levels; * Enhancing institutional and community capacity to prepare for and respond to climate-induced natural disasters; * Improving disaster risk management systems and practices (including early warning); * Enhancing government and community strategies to respond to drought exacerbated by climate change; * Establishing surveillance for heat early warning systems and response mechanisms.

- Coordination with relevant National Project progress reports

## Impact potential
UNEP welcomes ITAP’s positive assessment that the impact potential of the Project is high, which also highlights how its implementation will significantly respond to the climate information and early warning systems (CIWWS) needs and priorities of Timor-Leste identified in the baseline assessment and stakeholder consultations. This would in turn result in a more resilient society with better preparedness for climate change impacts.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 | PAGE 82 OF 116

The Project will contribute directly to Timor-Leste's achievement of progress towards these objectives.

## Engagement with civil society organisations

The Project will support an existing group of Government ministries and UN agencies responsible for coordinating disaster risk management, early warning coordination, and disaster risk reduction, expanding the group to include NGOs/CBOs and enabling the group to convey its message. The following agencies will be invited to establish a national focal point for climate services: National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) and IOM), international NGOs (including Mercy Corps, CARE, Oxfam, PLAN, World Vision, Caritas, and others), and other relevant organisations (CIVILIS*, NHFDC**, ASHRED***, FENAMET**** and others). Existing or ad-hoc early warning related work at the community level will be leveraged to support coordination and integration into a broader national system.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUNDING PROPOSAL V3.0 | PAGE 16

## Risks and barriers analysis:

The proposed Programme aims to overcome significant risks that currently hinder the scale-up of CSA practices and in Senegal. These represent significant obstacles to achieving sustainable agricultural development and climate change resilience in the country.

### Economic risks may limit the ability of financial institutions to offer concessional credit:
- The Senegalese economy continues to face headwinds as it recovers from the COVID-19 pandemic.
- The country is also facing geopolitical tensions, including (i) the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine; (ii) the imposition of restrictions on rice exports by India; (iii) the appreciation of the US dollar against the Senegalese CFA franc; and (iv) the global food price crisis, which have raised concerns about potential constraints on funding availability.

# DETAILED PROJECT / PROGRAMME DESCRIPTION

## GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL | PAGE 18 OF C

### Component 4: Enable the Government of Senegal to mainstream climate change adaptation and climate risk management into its safety net and social protection programs.

#### Output 4.1: By executing the project in collaboration with SECONSA (Secrétariat Exécutif du Conseil National de Sécurité Alimentaire), the project will support the Government of Senegal to build its capacity to scale up rural resilience and adaptation measures linked national social protection programs, supporting the government to implement its adaptation actions and eventual scaling-up.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V1.0 | PAGE 58

## Replicability

The participation of Senegalese financial institutions in climate finance is limited. Furthermore, there is limited uptake of existing climate-smart agriculture (CSA) financing schemes by the private sector in Senegal due to a limited capacity to structure and implement climate change initiatives.

### Sustainability

There is currently no sustained source of domestic private sector climate finance in Senegal due to a limited track record and capacity. The country has also been hit hard by overspent financial due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Global inflation, and deteriorating global security.

# APPRAISAL SUMMARY

## GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL | PAGE 59 OF 60

### Engagement with the NDA: In March 2016, a preliminary meeting was conducted with the GCF National Designated Authority (NDA) in Senegal, the Ministry of Environment, to present the project proposal and explore potential areas of collaboration. As a follow-up, in April 2016 the MOE, MOA, FAO, IFAD and other key stakeholders were invited to a joint discussion with the NDA on the concept note. In May 2016, the GCF Secretariat presented the draft project document to the NDA. In June 2016, the GCF Secretariat and the NDA jointly organized a workshop in Dakar. In July 2016, the GCF Secretariat and the NDA jointly organized another workshop in Dakar. In August 2016, the GCF Secretariat presented the GCF concept note to the inter-ministerial steering and technical committees. The institutional framework put in place by the NDA to examine the GCF concept note related to Senegal.

DERIVATION: over all 273 registry rows, take registry.canonical(doc,'gcf_funding_requested'); keep candidates with currency=='USD' AND value is not None (the parse guard that rejects a print whose mantissa and scale word contradict each other). 172 of 273 rows qualify. The maximum is FP241 'Financing Mitigation and Adaptation Projects (FMAP) in Indian MSMEs' (Small Industries Development Bank of India, B.39 2024), raw '2149 million USD' = 2,149,000,000 USD, p.5 section A.8. Double-attested: registry.json v1 carries the same string, and the VLM extraction data/extracted/vlm/qwen_qwen2.5-vl-7b/35_gcf-b39-02-add16-rev01-funding-proposal-package-fp241.md prints '## A.8 Total GCF funding requested' / '2149 million USD (multi-country proposals: clause 19 on annex 17)'. ROBUSTNESS CHECK: FP241 is the maximum under all three defensible inclusion rules - USD any section, USD template-A.8 only, and any-currency-including-unstamped - so this expectation does not depend on which guard the concurrent extremum mechanism implements. Runner-up is FP25 at 382.5 million USD, so the winner is not close. ROWS EXCLUDED, and why: the 19 rows whose canonical value is None because the printed unit is self-contradictory - FP162 '82,849 million USD', FP53 '31,385 million USD', FP18 '$37,460 million USD', FP199 '$36,232 million USD', FP45 '34,357 | million USD', FP153 '28,654 million USD', FP68 '27 054 | million USD', FP11 '$20,546,756 million USD', FP51 'US$ 17,346 million', FP23 '9,500,000 | million USD', FP75 '$5,000,000 million USD', FP3 '7,614,280 | million USD', FP270 '50 USD', FP168 '175.9 USD', FP115 'US$ 60.0', FP114 'US$12.95', plus EUR-side FP262, FP103, FP89. Read literally, six of those would outrank FP241 (FP162 alone would read as 82.8 billion), which is exactly the trap this case exists to catch - the mechanism must exclude them, and so does this expectation. Also excluded: 21 rows priced in EUR (largest FP117, 304 million EUR - not comparable without an FX rate the corpus does not carry) and 61 rows with no gcf_funding_requested candidate at all. Denominator for an honest answer: 172 of 273 rows state a comparable USD figure. No must_not_contain: a correct answer may legitimately quote an excluded ambiguous print while explaining why it was excluded, so any forbid on those numerals would punish the honest answer. docs [] - corpus-level, answerable only from a computed note; requiring retrieval to surface FP241's package from a question that never names it would measure the wrong thing.

FP270 describes implementation arrangements covering governance/oversight, roles across implementing institutions, procurement, and financial management/audit. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 42]

- **Project Steering Committee (PSC) for inter-ministerial coordination:** A PSC will be established to provide strategic oversight, decide on overall direction/priorities, and ensure alignment with the project’s vision and objectives, with decisions made by consensus. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 42]  
- **PSC chairing and membership:** The PSC will be chaired by the Minister of MOARM and include representation from NCDDSS, MEF, MOARM, NCODS, MOI, MAFF, MOE, and the Provincial Governor’s Office of Pursat. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 42]  

- **Component implementation split and coordination:** The proposal states that NDCDS will be responsible for implementing Component 4 and that there will be close technical coordination between MIDWDRAM and NDCDS to ensure synergies across components. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]  
- **Overall management and PMU responsibilities:** MOWRAM is described as responsible for overall management of the project, and the PMU is described as responsible for overall work plans and budgets, communications coordination, coordination with the NDCDS PIU on agriculture support activities, and implementing social and environmental safeguards (among other tasks). [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]  
- **PMU leadership and reporting line:** The PMU will be led by IFAD and will report to the Ministry of Economy and Finance/General Department of Resettlement (GEF-DR) to guide the resettlement path. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]  
- **Coordination at provincial level:** The PMU will coordinate with NDCDS and other implementing agencies at the provincial level and with service providers at the provincial level as required. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]  

- **Flow of funds and designated accounts:** The proposal indicates that designated accounts will be established for MOARM and NCODS, and that funds will be transferred directly by IFAD to MOARM and NCODS. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 42]  

- **Procurement staffing and responsibilities:** The NCDCDS PIU will have a procurement officer, procurement assistant, and procurement specialist, and MOIRWAM will be responsible for project procurement activities in Component 4. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 109]  
- **Procurement rules/tools and prior review:** A Contract Project Procurement Arrangement Letter (PALL) will set detailed procurement requirements and thresholds (including procurement methods and IFAD prior review of all contracts), and annual procurement plans aligned with the AWPBS require a PID “no objection” before procurement proceeds. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 109]  
- **Procurement monitoring systems:** The Project Implementation Plan (PIP) and Open Procurement Evaluation System (OPEN) will be used to prepare and monitor procurement implementation progress, and contracts will be registered in the IFAD Contract Management Tool (CMT). [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 109]  
- **National procurement context (Cambodia):** The proposal references Cambodia’s procurement framework, noting the General Directorate of Public Procurement (GDPP) administers the Law on Public Procurement and oversees implementation, while GIDICM oversees externally financed projects. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 108]  
- **Additional fiduciary/procurement mitigation measures:** The proposal lists measures such as using IFAD self-certification templates, contractor prequalification, requiring self-certification forms in bids/contracts, IFAD compliance screening of contractors/suppliers, and including procedures in the PIM to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing, with continuous monitoring of financial transactions by IFAD. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 103]  

- **Financial management controls and internal audit:** The proposal states that the PIM and Financial Management Manual will outline key FM arrangements/controls, and that the Internal Audit Department of MOWRAM and NCCD will conduct annual internal audits with outcomes shared with IFAD. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 110]  
- **Accounting and reporting approach:** PMU and PPU accounting procedures will follow SOPs for internationally funded projects, with electronic accounts maintained daily, based on IPSAS, using standard accounting software compatible with IFAD and other donors. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 110]  

- **Condition related to execution readiness:** The Board’s approval is described as potentially being subject to a condition that the Accredited Entity submit a certificate/legal opinion within 120 days confirming it has obtained final internal approvals and is prepared to proceed with implementation. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 136]

The project will provide water for the entire population of South Tarawa, estimated to be about 62,298 people in 2018, more than half of Kiribati's population, with a reliable, safe and climate resilient water supply. To achieve this, the project comprises:
